hints: Many words share their first few letters (lamp, lam, lamb). Could you store that shared beginning only once and reuse it?

Use a trie: every node has up to 26 child links (one per letter) and a boolean isEnd flag that marks where an inserted word finishes. search and startsWith both walk the same path; only search also checks the flag.

1. Root is an empty node.
  2. insert: for each letter, create the child if missing and move into it; at the end set isEnd = true.
  3. Write a helper walk(s) that follows letters and returns the last node, or null if a link is missing.
  4. search(word): node = walk(word); return node != null && node.isEnd.
  5. startsWith(prefix): return walk(prefix) != null.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Keep all inserted words in a list and compare each one letter by letter for every search or prefix check.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: A trie with a 26-slot child array per node: every operation touches only the letters of its own argument.

explain: Sample: insert lamp creates the path l→a→m→p and marks p as an end. search("lam") reaches the m node but its flag is false, so it returns false, while search("lamp") ends on a flagged node and returns true. startsWith("lam") only needs the path to exist, so it is true. After insert("lam") we simply set the flag on the existing m node, and now search("lam") is true. The key invariant: a path exists iff some inserted word has that prefix; the flag says whether a whole word ends there. Edge case: a prefix of an inserted word is not itself a word until it is inserted.
recognize: 'Insert words, then ask exact-match and begins-with questions' → store them in a trie (prefix tree).
